newsitem.title: CANADA: Pools buy UGG stake to block foreign buyer.
newsitem.headline: Pools buy UGG stake to block foreign buyer.

text.p: Two of Canada's largest privately held grain cooperatives upped their stake in United Grain Growers Ltd. to 13 percent of outstanding common shares to block any attempt by a foreign firm to take over UGG, Alberta Wheat Pool's chief financial officer told Reuters.
"We thought it was in our interests to keep UGG in Canadian hands so we increased our stake above 10 percent," AWP chief financial officer Geoff Southwood said.
Canadian laws allow whoever owns 90 percent of a company's outstanding shares to buy out minority shareholders, he noted.

Manitoba Pool Elevators and Alberta Wheat Pool, through jointly owned 3339351 Canada Ltd., said earlier it had increased its stock in UGG limited voting common shares to 1,616,700, or 13 percent, on Wednesday from 999,700.
UGG shares closed at C$11.70 each on the Toronto Stock Exchange Wednesday, they rose C$0.65 to C$12.35 at 1315 EST Thursday with 7,768 shares changing hands.
Asked if MPE and AWP may try to take over UGG, Southwood said: "It's always a possibility but right now we want to talk with UGG and ensure it remains in Canadian hands."
MPE delegates will vote on that firm's strategy vis-a-vis UGG at its annual Spring meeting at the end of February, MPE president Charlie Swanson said.
The meeting is closed to the public.
Both cooperatives shared an equal amount in the cost of acquiring the additional UGG shares but neither would disclose the dollar value.
"This is an unexpected development. It's recent enough that we need time to assess it fully. As a publicly traded company, there's not much more I can say," UGG chief executive Brian Hayward said.
Rumours in the past year have named Nebraska-based multinational food processor ConAgra, among others, as a potential suitor.

UGG held a 17 percent share of Canada's grain handling market in fiscal 1996 (Aug/July). This has been cited by industry observers as an attractive feature to foreign processors wishing to ensure certainty of supply.

UGG has also taken a leading position in building concrete large volume country elevators to expedite its just-in-time delivery system before Canada cut its 98-year-old rail transportation subsidy August 1, 1995.
